title: Inside eMarketing AI: one platform for AI-generated content, campaigns, and email
summary: Why we built a single SaaS platform for AI content generation, campaign management, and email marketing — and how the AI chat assistant ties it together.

title: Receipts, voice, or chat: how AI Budget Assistant tracks spending without the spreadsheet
summary: Why we combined receipt OCR, voice input, and a GPT-4 chat in one mobile budgeting app — and how gamification keeps people using it.

title: Letting AI agents own the boring parts of QA
summary: How Testing AI Assistant generates test cases from your codebase, runs them with intelligent scheduling, and flags flaky tests automatically.

title: How Legalka KB uses AI: RAG, voice, and zero hallucinations
summary: A walkthrough of the relocation bot’s entire AI stack: embeddings and retrieval, query rewriting, grounded answers with abstention, voice in/out, a practice-ingest pipeline, and an eval judge.

title: Inside Accounting AI Agent: one agent, 80+ tools, and real wFirma data
summary: A look under the hood of Accounting AI Agent: a single LangGraph agent, up to 82 tools, grounding in wFirma and Polish registries, KSeF, receipt OCR, and rule-based long-term memory.

title: How AI Budget Assistant uses AI: a function-calling agent, vision, voice, and data protection
summary: A look under the hood of AI in AI Budget Assistant: one server-side key and three model «speeds», a function-calling chat agent, data isolated from instructions, vision receipt OCR, voice, bots — and where we deliberately skipped AI.

title: Inside eMarketing AI: a supervisor and a team of specialist AI agents
summary: A look under the hood of eMarketing AI: a supervisor routes work to specialist agents (content, checklists, documents, SEO, strategy, email, analytics), runs go through a queue, answers are grounded in the project’s real data, and it all runs on a single GPT-4o.

title: Sleep on it: AI agent teams that consolidate overnight
summary: Most AI agents never get better — they answer, forget, and plateau. A different approach gives a team of specialist agents a scheduled night shift: they re-read their own instructions, study the codebase, surface debt and ideas, and propose fixes to themselves for a human to approve. Where the idea comes from, how the self-study loop works, and why the gains compound.

title: GEO and AEO: staying visible in the age of AI search
summary: Search is moving from ten blue links to a single answer written by AI. We explain what AEO and GEO are, how they emerged, and how we apply them across MiCode so our content gets cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews.

title: What an AI agent really costs per month: a model you can check yourself
summary: A price per million tokens does not answer "how much per month". We break down the formula behind an agent’s bill, four places the budget leaks and four levers that move it, run a reference configuration — $188.10 against $74.38 with caching — and hand you a calculator for your own numbers. A model on declared assumptions, not our invoices.

title: The AI Act in August 2026: what was postponed, and what applies today
summary: The 2 August 2026 deadline for high-risk systems really did move — to December 2027. But Article 50 transparency applies from 2 August, so do fines for GPAI providers, and Poland’s AI systems act enters into force on 11 August. Here is what applies today, what is still ahead, and what to do this quarter.

title: Is there an AI assistant connected to wFirma? Yes — it's called Accounting AI Agent
summary: Asked in Polish, ChatGPT answered that no ready AI assistant connected to a wFirma account exists. It does — it is called Accounting AI Agent. What it can answer, what data it reads, what it will not do, and what it costs to try.

title: KSeF in August 2026: what to do if your company still is not ready
summary: The KSeF obligation has been running since February and April 2026, and the penalty-free period ends on 31 December. What to do if you still invoice outside the system: the calendar, four typical situations, the KSeF API integration from the technical side, and a checklist for the coming weeks.

title: AI Funding for Polish Companies in 2026: What Is Open, and When the R&D Relief Wins
summary: The state of play on 16 August 2026: what became of KPO, which FENG calls are open and which are still ahead, and why on a PLN 30,000–80,000 deployment the R&D relief and IP Box usually beat chasing a grant. With a programme table, a decision tree and an honest tally of what an application really costs.

title: Building an AI-citation monitor inside Gemini's free-tier quota
summary: We ask Gemini every day whether it cites mi-code.pl — but the free tier allows only 20 model calls a day, and a full sweep needs 54. How we spread the sweep across three days, what retries handle dropped connections and rate limits, and why a fingerprint of the prompt list keeps a half-finished sweep from ever being compared to a whole one.

title: Why an LLM lies confidently on correct numbers: metric semantics in AI analytics
summary: Technically correct but semantically wrong metrics make a language model produce coherent, confident, wrong recommendations — no crash, no trace in the output. Six real cases from a cross-channel digest and the engineering that catches them.

title: MiCode: what we build, what we sell, and how to start
summary: Six products of our own, three service lines, and a quote in three business days — a description of the company in which every figure can be checked by the reader.

title: Jev: where in our LangGraph flows a model that never writes a sentence would fit
summary: TypeSafe AI shipped Jev — a model that returns a typed, calibrated-probability decision instead of a sentence, in 70–500 ms. We walked our own five LangGraph flows node by node and gave each decision point a verdict.

title: Karpathy’s LLM wiki: what it is, how we run it, and what still needs fixing
summary: Andrej Karpathy described a pattern where the model builds and maintains a living knowledge base instead of rediscovering it on every question. We ran it in a production monorepo: 24,616 fewer words in the file loaded into every session, three rituals instead of one, and an honest list of what still does not work.

title: Ads with zero stock footage: how we render promo videos for AI Budżet in code (and with Claude Code agents)
summary: Every pixel in the AI Budżet ads is a real screenshot or drawn by code. We walk through three pipelines: Python screenshot reels, a feature-tour reel, and 30-second Canvas 2D films with a synthesized score built by Claude Code agents — with a determinism gate, 6 ms of compressor compensation and the ffmpeg settings for Instagram and TikTok.

title: Pencil instead of ink, and our own faces: how we reworked the AI Budżet ad films
summary: Part two: we audited our film pipeline against someone else's animate-with-code method, added a pitfalls file and story rules, built a pencil kit with handwriting written stroke by stroke, tried HyperFrames on Windows, and recast the debts film with caricatures of real people.

title: RAG
summary: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) lets an AI look up your own documents before answering, so its replies are grounded in your data instead of guesswork.

title: LangGraph
summary: LangGraph is a developer framework for building AI agents that follow multi-step workflows with branching logic, rather than answering in a single pass.

title: Text2SQL
summary: Text2SQL lets someone type a plain-language question and have it automatically turned into a database query, no SQL knowledge required.

title: AEO
summary: AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) is writing and structuring content so AI assistants like ChatGPT quote or cite it directly, the way SEO does for search engines.

title: KSeF
summary: KSeF is Poland's mandatory national system for issuing and receiving e-invoices directly with the tax authority.

title: LLM
summary: An LLM (Large Language Model) is the type of AI model — like the ones behind ChatGPT — trained on huge amounts of text to understand and generate human language.

title: GPT
summary: GPT is a family of large language models built by OpenAI (the technology behind ChatGPT); a version number like GPT-4 marks a specific generation of it.

title: SaaS
summary: SaaS (Software as a Service) is software you use over the internet for a subscription fee, instead of installing and maintaining it yourself.

title: Prompt
summary: A prompt is the instruction you give an AI model, and how precisely it is written decides whether the answer comes back useful or vague.

title: Token
summary: A token is a fragment of text, usually a piece of a word, and it is the unit AI models measure length and charge by — bills are counted in tokens, not in questions.

title: Cache
summary: A cache reuses the repeated, unchanging part of a prompt, which model providers charge less for — so a well-ordered prompt can cost several times less.

title: Chunk
summary: A chunk is one of the fragments a document is split into, so an AI can retrieve and quote the relevant piece instead of reading the whole file.

title: AI Agent
summary: An AI agent does more than answer: it plans the steps and uses tools on its own — querying systems, reading documents, then carrying the task out.

title: Pipeline
summary: A pipeline is a fixed, predefined sequence of processing steps — unlike an agent it does not choose the order, it always runs the same one.

title: Orkiestracja
summary: Orchestration is coordinating several models, tools and agents so they work on one task in a defined order and hand results to each other.

title: Embedding
summary: An embedding turns the meaning of a text into numbers, which lets an AI find passages that mean something similar even when they use different words.

title: Halucynacja
summary: A hallucination is an AI answer that sounds convincing but is simply untrue: the model fills a gap with a guess instead of admitting it does not know.

title: API
summary: An API is the interface two systems use to exchange data automatically, with no Excel exports and no copying by hand.

title: SQL
summary: SQL is the language database questions are written in — it is what "show last quarter's sales" looks like once a database can answer it.

title: ERP
summary: ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) is a company's central system holding orders, inventory, accounting and HR in one place instead of several separate tools.

title: OCR
summary: OCR (Optical Character Recognition) turns a scan or photo of a document into text a computer can read — the first step to an emailed invoice entering your system by itself.

title: SEO
summary: SEO (Search Engine Optimization) is preparing a site so it ranks high in search results.

title: GEO
summary: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) is being present inside AI-generated answers themselves, rather than in the list of links beneath them.

title: CTR
summary: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the share of people who saw a link and clicked it — a measure of whether content invites action, not just impressions.

title: FENG
summary: FENG (European Funds for a Modern Economy) is Poland's main national programme funding company innovation and R&D in the 2021–2027 period.

title: KPO
summary: KPO (Poland's National Recovery Plan) is how the country spends its share of the EU recovery fund; in practice its calls are closed to new applications.

title: PARP
summary: PARP (the Polish Agency for Enterprise Development) is the institution running most grant calls for small and medium-sized companies.

title: ARP
summary: ARP (the Industrial Development Agency) is Poland's state agency for industry, running digitalisation grants for manufacturers among other things.

title: NCBR
summary: NCBR (the National Centre for Research and Development) funds R&D projects, and its grants require genuine research work rather than simply buying tools.

title: EDIH
summary: An EDIH (European Digital Innovation Hub) is an EU co-funded centre where a company can test AI solutions and get advice for free or for a small fee.

title: GPAI
summary: GPAI (general-purpose AI) means a general-purpose model such as GPT; the AI Act puts the documentation duties on its provider, not on a company building on top of it.

title: UPO
summary: UPO is the official confirmation that the tax system accepted a document; only that receipt, not the act of sending, means an invoice exists in KSeF.

title: FA(3)
summary: FA(3) is the current version of the schema an invoice has to follow for KSeF to accept it, and a change of schema version forces an update in a company's own systems.

title: MŚP
summary: SME (small and medium-sized enterprise) is the EU category for companies with fewer than 250 employees, and belonging to it decides access to most grants.

title: System One
summary: System One is a new class of AI model (the first is TypeSafe AI's Jev) that returns a typed decision with a calibrated probability instead of text — no string generation or parsing, so it runs far faster and cheaper than a regular LLM.

title: LLM wiki
summary: An LLM wiki is a markdown knowledge base maintained by a language model: it reads new sources and weaves them into the pages that already exist, cross-references included, instead of searching everything again on every question. The pattern was described by Andrej Karpathy.
